bib.title: BBQ: A Hand-Built Bias Benchmark for Question Answering
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2022, pages 2086-2105

read.skipped: Figure data (numeric heat-map cells, pp. 8-20) skimmed only; read as noise.

question: How do social biases against protected classes manifest in the discrete outputs of question-answering models, and when do they override a correct answer?
hypothesis: Models will rely on social stereotypes when the context is under-informative, and biases may also lower accuracy when the correct answer conflicts with a stereotype.
contributions: BBQ, a hand-written dataset of 58,492 examples over nine social bias categories plus two intersectional categories, validated by crowdworkers
A bias score metric computed separately for ambiguous and disambiguated contexts
Evaluation of UnifiedQA, RoBERTa and DeBERTaV3 showing reliance on stereotypes in ambiguous contexts

method.summary: Authors hand-write 325 templates, each targeting an attested bias, expanded into 58,492 three-choice QA examples in sets of four (ambiguous or disambiguated context x negative or non-negative question). Models answer zero-shot (UnifiedQA) or after RACE fine-tuning (RoBERTa, DeBERTaV3); accuracy and a bias score are computed per category and context.
method.task: multiple-choice question answering for social bias measurement

datasets.name: BBQ
datasets.size: 58,492 examples; 325 templates, about 175 questions per template on average; at least 25 templates per category; 8 to 200 examples per template
datasets.split: no split; all used for evaluation
datasets.preprocessing: Each template validated on MTurk: 5 annotators per item, 4/5 must match gold label, failing templates edited and re-validated. UNKNOWN answer sampled from 10 equivalent strings. Order of target and non-target permuted.

datasets.name: RACE
datasets.preprocessing: Used to fine-tune RoBERTa and DeBERTaV3 for multiple choice

other.note: zero-shot, no prior exposure to BBQ; trained on eight datasets

training.objective: multiple-choice QA fine-tuning on RACE (RoBERTa, DeBERTaV3 only)

other.scope: applies to RoBERTa and DeBERTaV3 only; UnifiedQA is used as released

inference.decoding: UnifiedQA outputs a string; scored by exact match between top output and each answer option
inference.samples: inferred: one run per model, no seeds or repeats reported
inference.prompting: zero-shot; context, question and three answer options in RACE-style or ARC-style input format; exact templates not printed

other.unknown_strings: UNKNOWN option sampled from 10 strings: can't answer, can't be determined, cannot answer, cannot be determined, not answerable, not enough info, not enough information, not known, undetermined, unknown
other.excluded: 3 examples (0.005%) excluded because UnifiedQA output matched no option

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: per category and context (ambiguous, disambiguated); in disambiguated further split by whether correct answer aligns with the bias

baselines: Human accuracy on 300 sampled examples + 50 filler items
eval.protocol: Single run per model; no significance tests. Human accuracy by MTurk, 5 raters, raw and majority vote.

limits: Bias scores near zero do not prove a model is unbiased: only 25 templates per category.
Only US English-speaking cultural contexts; not valid for other cultures or very different text domains.
Measures discrete outputs, so it will miss biases UnQover's likelihood approach catches (authors concede).
Names are an imperfect proxy for race and gender.
Single-template results are noisy (Table 2 is 72 examples).
Intersectional results inconsistent; no conclusion possible.
Only fine-tuned/QA-specific models (UnifiedQA, RoBERTa, DeBERTaV3) tested; no prompted generative LLMs, no prompt variants, no seeds or repeated runs.
RoBERTa-Base favors UNKNOWN regardless of context; authors do not explain.

terms.definition: A context missing the information needed to answer; the correct answer is always the UNKNOWN option.
Adds information identifying which individual answers the negative or non-negative question; the correct answer is always one of the two individuals.
The percent of non-UNKNOWN outputs that align with a social bias; 0% means no bias measured, 100% all answers align, -100% all go against.
